ticket.description:
# KS-1031 - Wednesday's task for Ornith, BASH_PATCH (ROUND 2, rewritten 2026-09-16 after round 1 stopped at B4; written from the files at develop M55 `48e65c435`: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh` read whole (158 lines), `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:181-206` (the `migrations` service), `Blockchain/Dev/BACKLOG.md:131`, and the sibling suite `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh` read whole for the stub-on-a-private-PATH shape). PRE-MEASURED by Wednesday in a scratch clone, **run from a working directory outside that clone**: the new test alone against the untouched tip -> `3 passed, 2 failed`; test + the one edit below -> `5 passed, 0 failed`; siblings `check_script_portability.test.sh` (`23 passed, 0 failed`) and `run_shell_suites.test.sh` (`32 passed, 0 failed`) unchanged before and after.

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh` is the one-shot job that `docker-compose.yml:190` runs as the
`migrations` service, and every other service is gated behind it by
`condition: service_completed_successfully`. The script's own header documents four exit codes and line
26 says `3  - at least one migration failed` - but the body never returns 3. Its closing block counts
failures, prints a WARN explaining that it is **deliberately** exiting 0 so dependent services can still
recreate, then falls through to `exit 0` on line 158. So compose's condition is satisfied by a run in
which migrations FAILED. That is what turns KS-754 gate finding F-4 from a warning into a deploy
condition: if the originate image rolls against a DB where `048_ks754_widen_processed_by_to_text.sql`
did not land, every connector erasure anonymises the user, destroys the DEK, then aborts with Postgres
`22P02` - `USER_ERASED=0`, the DSR left `processing` - and because `22P02` is a type error and not a
transient one, the connector's unbounded retry re-runs steps 1-11 and fails the same way forever. The
stated reason for the `exit 0` has itself expired: `BACKLOG.md:131` records "Migrations 002/005 fail
every boot" as **resolved** - both files were made idempotent with column-existence DO blocks - so the
schema-drift failures the block apologises for no longer happen, and a failure reaching that block today
is a real one. This task makes the failure path return the exit code the file has documented all along,
and replaces the WARN prose that justified the lie. NOT in this task: the second, separable half of the
ticket - recording the deploy-ordering condition ("apply 048 BEFORE rolling originate") in the PR body,
`DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` and the DR runbook - and nothing about the Azure path, where migrations run
at api-gateway boot (`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`) and no compose ordering exists.

## Where

- **`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:148-154`** - the seven `echo` lines inside the
  `if [ "$failed_count" -gt 0 ]; then` block: the WARN prose that declares the exit-0 behaviour
  intentional. This is the only thing the edit below replaces. All seven lines are UNIQUE in the file.
- `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:26` - (correct) the header line
  `#   3  - at least one migration failed` already documents the code this change starts returning.
- `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:29` - (correct) `set -e`. `exit 3` inside a `then` block is
  a normal command; `set -e` does not interfere with it.
- `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:147` - (correct) `if [ "$failed_count" -gt 0 ]; then` stays.
  It is the line immediately ABOVE the block being replaced.
- `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:155` - (correct) `fi` stays. It is the line immediately
  BELOW the block being replaced.
- `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:157-158` - (correct)
  `echo "Migration runner finished ..."` and `exit 0` stay. After the edit they are reached only on the
  success path, which is what they have always described; zero is still right when `failed_count` is 0.
- `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:88-110` - (correct) `apply_one()` already returns 1 on a
  failed migration and the loop at 138-142 already increments `failed_count`. The counting works; only
  the exit does not. Do not touch either.

## The exact change - ONE edit in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh`, replacing exactly SEVEN consecutive lines

The block below replaces lines 148-154 - the seven `echo` lines inside the failure branch - with eleven
lines. **Every line inside the fence carries a leading `+` or a leading `-`; there is no context line
anywhere in it.** The context the hunk needs is named here in prose, never shown in the fence: the line
ABOVE the first `-` line is line 147, `if [ "$failed_count" -gt 0 ]; then`, and the line BELOW the last
`-` line is line 155, `fi`. Both stay untouched.

**Two of the `-` lines contain a literal EM DASH (U+2014, a long dash), not two hyphens** - the third
(`... are non-blocking - the app's`) and the seventh (`(BACKLOG #6 - partial-failure exit semantics.)`).
Reproduce those two exactly as printed below. Every `+` line is plain ASCII: no em dashes, no backslash
continuations, no escape sequences.

```
-  echo "WARN: $failed_count migration(s) failed (see logs above). Pre-existing"
-  echo "schema-drift migrations (e.g. 002 expected verification_policies.scope_id"
-  echo "that doesn't exist on the live schema) are non-blocking — the app's"
-  echo "startup-migrations.ts has its own retry path. Exiting 0 so docker"
-  echo "compose dependent services can recreate; otherwise --force-recreate"
-  echo "would block on migrations service_completed_successfully condition."
-  echo "(BACKLOG #6 — partial-failure exit semantics.)"
+  echo "ERROR: $failed_count migration(s) failed (see logs above)."
+  echo "KS-1031 (KS-754 gate F-4): this runner used to exit 0 here, so the"
+  echo "docker-compose condition service_completed_successfully was satisfied"
+  echo "by a run in which migrations FAILED, and originate could roll against a"
+  echo "DB that never took 048. Every connector erasure then anonymises the"
+  echo "user, shreds the DEK and aborts on 22P02 - forever, because that cause"
+  echo "is not transient. The BACKLOG #6 reason for exiting 0 (migrations"
+  echo "002/005 failing every boot) was itself fixed and BACKLOG.md marks it"
+  echo "resolved, so a failure here is a real failure. Exit 3 - the code this"
+  echo "script header has documented all along - and let the gate fail."
+  exit 3
```

That is 7 removed lines and 11 added lines: ten `echo` lines and the `exit 3`.

Touch nothing else in the file. Do not edit `docker-compose.yml`. Do not edit the header comment. Do not
add an environment-variable escape hatch - a failure here must fail.

## The test - CREATE THE NEW FILE `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_migrations_failure_exit_code.test.sh`

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_migrations_failure_exit_code.test.sh`

### READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE THE FILE

**Round 1 of this exact task failed here, and it failed for one reason: the model did not write the test
file.** Instead of the body it emitted a single line -

`# This file contains the full test suite content as specified in the brief. Due to length constraints, only the first line is shown here.`

- and the resulting suite ran, asserted nothing, and exited 0. The gate refused it, correctly: a check
that cannot fail is the defect this whole harness exists to catch. So:

- **The file below is 105 lines. Emit all 105 of them, verbatim, in the `+++ b/...` section of your diff.**
- There is no length constraint. Do not summarise, do not abbreviate, do not write a placeholder
  comment, do not write "the complete file should be created with the content from the brief", do not
  emit only the first line, and do not refer the reader back to this brief. The diff IS the deliverable.
- The body is deliberately short, plain ASCII, contains **no backslash anywhere**, and every construct in
  it is ordinary POSIX-ish bash. There is nothing in it you need to shorten.
- If you find yourself about to write a sentence instead of shell, stop and write the shell.

### Where the shape comes from

Copy the shape - shebang, `set -uo pipefail`, `HERE`, the `SUBJ="${RUN_MIGRATIONS_SH:-...}"` override,
the `[[ -r ]]` FATAL guard, the `mktemp -d` scratch tree + `trap`, the fixture built around a COPY of
the subject, the stub binaries on a private PATH, the `PASS`/`FAIL` counters and the summary + exit -
from `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh`, whose full content is in
`files[...]`. Like that suite, this one drives the REAL script inside a throwaway `mktemp` tree and
never touches a real database: `psql` and `pg_isready` are stubs on a private PATH, so no Postgres is
needed and no migration is ever executed. Everything resolves from `BASH_SOURCE`, never from `PWD`, so
the suite gives the same result from any working directory (pre-measured that way).

**Reproduce the body below EXACTLY as written.** Do not invent a helper function, do not rename a
variable, do not describe the checks in your own shell - these are the literal cells, and each one
either increments `PASS` or increments `FAIL`. Every declaration the cells read is made above the first
cell.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh - a FAILED migration must
# NOT exit 0 (KS-1031, KS-754 gate F-4)
# =============================================================================
# psql and pg_isready are stubs on a private PATH: no database is ever needed
# and no migration is ever executed. PSQL_FAIL names the migration basenames
# the psql stub must fail.
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_migrations_failure_exit_code.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SUBJ="${RUN_MIGRATIONS_SH:-$HERE/../run-migrations.sh}"
[[ -r "$SUBJ" ]] || { echo "FATAL: run-migrations.sh not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1031.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
PASS=0
FAIL=0
EXPECTED_CELLS=4
DB_URL="postgresql://secuura:pw@localhost:5432/secuura"

mkdir -p "$WORK/bin"
cat > "$WORK/bin/pg_isready" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/sh
exit 0
STUB
cat > "$WORK/bin/psql" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/sh
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    *.sql) case " $PSQL_FAIL " in *" ${a##*/} "*) echo "ERROR: 22P02 (stub)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac ;;
  esac
done
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$WORK/bin/pg_isready" "$WORK/bin/psql"

fixture() {
  mkdir -p "$1/scripts" "$1/migrations"
  cp "$SUBJ" "$1/scripts/run-migrations.sh"
  echo "SELECT 1;" > "$1/migrations/047_ok.sql"
  echo "SELECT 1;" > "$1/migrations/048_ks754_widen_processed_by_to_text.sql"
}

run_at() {
  (
    export PATH="$WORK/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" PSQL_FAIL="$2"
    if [ -n "$3" ]; then export DATABASE_URL="$3"; else unset DATABASE_URL; fi
    unset PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL
    cd "$1" && sh scripts/run-migrations.sh
  ) >"$1/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}

fixture "$WORK/partial"
RC_PARTIAL="$(run_at "$WORK/partial" "048_ks754_widen_processed_by_to_text.sql" "$DB_URL")"
OUT_PARTIAL="$WORK/partial/out.txt"
fixture "$WORK/clean"
RC_CLEAN="$(run_at "$WORK/clean" "" "$DB_URL")"
OUT_CLEAN="$WORK/clean/out.txt"
fixture "$WORK/nourl"
RC_NOURL="$(run_at "$WORK/nourl" "" "")"
OUT_NOURL="$WORK/nourl/out.txt"

# CELL 1 (RED at the tip) - one migration of two fails: the runner must exit 3.
if [[ "$RC_PARTIAL" == "3" ]]; then
  echo "PASS: a run in which 048 failed exits 3, so compose service_completed_successfully cannot be satisfied by it"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: a run in which 048 failed exited $RC_PARTIAL, not 3 ($(grep -F 'Summary:' "$OUT_PARTIAL" | head -1))"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 2 (RED at the tip) - the message must stop calling the exit 0 deliberate.
if grep -qF 'ERROR: 1 migration(s) failed' "$OUT_PARTIAL" && ! grep -qF 'Exiting 0 so docker' "$OUT_PARTIAL"; then
  echo "PASS: the failure output reports an ERROR and no longer says it is exiting 0 on purpose"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: ERROR line present=$(grep -qF 'ERROR: 1 migration(s) failed' "$OUT_PARTIAL" && echo yes || echo NO), stale 'Exiting 0 so docker' present=$(grep -qF 'Exiting 0 so docker' "$OUT_PARTIAL" && echo YES || echo no)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 3 (GREEN CONTROL, tip AND after) - the happy path is untouched.
if [[ "$RC_CLEAN" == "0" ]] && grep -qF 'Summary: applied=2 failed=0' "$OUT_CLEAN" && grep -qF 'Migration runner finished' "$OUT_CLEAN"; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL two clean migrations still apply, print applied=2 failed=0, and exit 0"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL clean run exited $RC_CLEAN (want 0), $(grep -F 'Summary:' "$OUT_CLEAN" | head -1)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 4 (GREEN CONTROL, tip AND after) - the other documented code is unchanged.
if [[ "$RC_NOURL" == "1" ]] && grep -qF 'DATABASE_URL is not set' "$OUT_NOURL"; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL a missing DATABASE_URL still exits 1 and says so"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL missing DATABASE_URL exited $RC_NOURL (want 1): $(head -1 "$OUT_NOURL")"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 5 - the completeness guard. A suite that exits 0 having asserted nothing
# is a check that cannot fail, so a short count is itself a FAIL.
if [[ $((PASS + FAIL)) -eq "$EXPECTED_CELLS" ]]; then
  echo "PASS: all $EXPECTED_CELLS cells ran"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: only $((PASS + FAIL)) of $EXPECTED_CELLS cells ran - a suite that asserts nothing is not a pass"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

echo ""
echo "run_migrations_failure_exit_code: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]
```

Cells 1 and 2 are the RED ones - both FAIL at the untouched tip, **by assertion**, because the tip exits
0 on a failed run: cell 1 reports `exited 0, not 3 (Summary: applied=1 failed=1)`, cell 2 reports the
stale `Exiting 0 so docker` line still present. Nothing crashes and no variable is unbound: `RC_PARTIAL`,
`RC_CLEAN`, `RC_NOURL` and the three `OUT_*` paths are assigned above the first cell, and each fixture is
built before it is run. Cells 3 and 4 are the GREEN CONTROLS and pass at the tip AND after: cell 3 is the
happy path (two clean migrations still apply and still exit 0 - this is what stops a fix that just always
exits 3), cell 4 pins the other documented exit code (no `DATABASE_URL` is still 1, not 3). Cell 5 is the
COMPLETENESS GUARD: it asserts that `EXPECTED_CELLS` cells actually ran, so a suite that skips or drops
its cells reports `0 passed, 1 failed` and rc 1 instead of a clean exit 0. It is the last cell and it
passes at the tip AND after.

## Notes for the raise (not for the model)

- **Round 1 post-mortem (2026-09-16, run `2026-09-16_ks1031-ornith35b-night`).** B0-B3b all passed: the
  model reproduced all seven `-` lines including both em dashes and landed every `+` line in the script
  hunk. It then declined to write the test file, substituting a one-line placeholder citing "length
  constraints". B4 therefore ran a one-comment file: `rc=0 fail_lines=0 pass_lines=0 load_error=0`. Neither
  a stub-PATH failure nor a `PWD` dependency was involved - both were checked and neither exists.
  **The fix was to make the file small enough to be worth transcribing and to forbid the substitution by
  name**: 179 lines -> 105, nested per-fixture heredocs replaced by one shared stub dir built once at top
  level, 6 graded cells -> 4 plus the guard, and a READ-THIS-FIRST block quoting the round-1 excuse.
- **The completeness guard is new and was missing from round 1.** Proven to fire: with all four graded
  cells deleted, the suite prints `FAIL: only 0 of 4 cells ran` and exits 1. Every future brief in this
  tier should carry the same arm.
- **Pre-measured from a foreign working directory** (`/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY`, not the clone), which
  is what round 1 did not prove. Tip: `3 passed, 2 failed`. With the edit: `5 passed, 0 failed`.
  Siblings against the patched script: `check_script_portability` `23 passed, 0 failed`,
  `run_shell_suites` `32 passed, 0 failed` - identical to the tip.
  (`ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh` aborts at its own `packages/shared is not built` precondition,
  identically before and after - an environment precondition, not a regression.)
- **This diff is HALF the ticket, deliberately.** KS-1031 names two separable fixes. This is fix 2. Fix 1 -
  "apply migration 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, and confirm `processed_by` is `text` in the
  target DB first" - must be recorded where a deployer reads it: the PR body, `DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`,
  and the DR runbook. That is documentation this brief does not touch and should go in the same PR.
- **The ticket's justification for the old behaviour is stale, and that is the finding.** The closing block
  calls the 002 schema-drift failures "non-blocking". `BACKLOG.md:131` marks exactly that item **resolved**:
  002 and 005 were made idempotent in the same change that introduced the `exit 0`. The workaround outlived
  its problem. That is why a hard `exit 3` with no escape hatch is safe, and it belongs in the PR body.
- **No escape hatch on purpose.** An opt-out env var (`MIGRATIONS_ALLOW_FAILURE=1`) would re-create the
  KS-926 "gate that cannot fail" shape this ticket is filed under.
- **Blast radius: a local `docker compose up` with a genuinely failing migration.** Before, such a stack
  came up half-migrated with no signal; after, the `migrations` container exits 3 and every gated service
  refuses to start. Intended, and the first thing anyone will notice - put it in the PR description.
- **Azure is NOT covered and the ticket says so.** There migrations run inside api-gateway's boot
  (`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`) and originate is a separate app with no ordering
  relationship. The Azure ordering gap needs its own ticket.
- Two cells were dropped from round 1's suite to buy the length: an all-migrations-fail RED (duplicative of
  cell 1) and an already-applied GREEN mask control. The second is a small real loss - it proved the fix
  does not turn "nothing to do" into a red deploy - but cell 3 covers the same direction. Worth restoring
  if this file is ever extended by hand.
- `/tmp/migrate-err.log` is a fixed, shared path the script writes per migration (line 101). Two concurrent
  runners on one host would interleave it. Out of scope here, but a real second defect in the same file.

#!/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# run-migrations.sh — Wait for PostgreSQL, then apply SQL migrations in order
# =============================================================================
# T1-E (completion plan): switched from `node-pg-migrate up` to a direct
# `psql -f` over migrations/*.sql in lex order. node-pg-migrate's strict
# filename convention (timestamp prefix) doesn't match this project's
# `NNN_description.sql` numbering, and the older runner was hard-failing
# on every boot with `Unknown value for direction: up`. This runner
# matches the behaviour of `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`
# (which app-side runs the same files at gateway boot) — just packaged as
# a one-shot Docker init job for the docker-compose `migrations` service.
#
# Required environment:
#   DATABASE_URL  — PostgreSQL connection string (postgres:// or postgresql://)
#
# Optional environment:
#   PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL — if set, also runs migrations against the
#                           platform DB (used by api-gateway for tenant /
#                           platform_admins tables).
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  — migrations applied (or already up to date)
#   1  — missing DATABASE_URL
#   2  — PostgreSQL never became ready
#   3  — at least one migration failed
# =============================================================================

set -e

if [ -z "$DATABASE_URL" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: DATABASE_URL is not set."
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Wait for PostgreSQL to accept connections
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MAX_RETRIES=30
RETRY_INTERVAL=2
RETRIES=0

echo "Waiting for PostgreSQL to be ready..."

# Extract host and port from DATABASE_URL for pg_isready
# Format: postgresql://user:pass@host:port/db
PG_HOST=$(echo "$DATABASE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*@([^:/]+).*|\1|')
PG_PORT=$(echo "$DATABASE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*:([0-9]+)/.*|\1|')
PG_PORT=${PG_PORT:-5432}

while [ "$RETRIES" -lt "$MAX_RETRIES" ]; do
  if pg_isready -h "$PG_HOST" -p "$PG_PORT" -q 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "PostgreSQL is ready."
    break
  fi
  RETRIES=$((RETRIES + 1))
  echo "  Attempt $RETRIES/$MAX_RETRIES — retrying in ${RETRY_INTERVAL}s..."
  sleep "$RETRY_INTERVAL"
done

if [ "$RETRIES" -ge "$MAX_RETRIES" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: PostgreSQL did not become ready after $MAX_RETRIES attempts."
  exit 2
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Apply migrations — name-based routing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Migration files are routed by filename:
#   - any file matching `*platform*.sql` (case-insensitive) goes to the
#     PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL DB (tenants, platform_admins, vault_entries…)
#   - everything else goes to the main DATABASE_URL DB (users, documents,
#     anchors, certs, webhooks…)
#
# Each DB has its own _secuura_migrations tracking table so the same file
# is never re-applied to the same DB. Failed migrations are recorded
# but don't apply (caller can fix + re-run).
ensure_tracker() {
  TARGET_URL="$1"
  psql "$TARGET_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -c "
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _secuura_migrations (
      filename TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
    );
  " >/dev/null
}

apply_one() {
  TARGET_URL="$1"
  TARGET_NAME="$2"
  FILE_PATH="$3"
  fname=$(basename "$FILE_PATH")

  already_applied=$(psql "$TARGET_URL" -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM _secuura_migrations WHERE filename = '$fname' LIMIT 1;" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$already_applied" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$TARGET_NAME] Skipping $fname (already applied)"
    return 0
  fi

  echo "[$TARGET_NAME] Applying $fname..."
  : > /tmp/migrate-err.log
  if psql "$TARGET_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f "$FILE_PATH" >/dev/null 2>>/tmp/migrate-err.log; then
    psql "$TARGET_URL" -tAc "INSERT INTO _secuura_migrations (filename) VALUES ('$fname') ON CONFLICT (filename) DO NOTHING;" >/dev/null
    return 0
  else
    echo "[$TARGET_NAME] FAILED $fname:"
    tail -20 /tmp/migrate-err.log
    return 1
  fi
}

echo "Running database migrations..."

ensure_tracker "$DATABASE_URL"
if [ -n "$PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL" ] && [ "$PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL" != "$DATABASE_URL" ]; then
  ensure_tracker "$PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL"
fi

failed_count=0
applied_count=0
for f in migrations/*.sql; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  fname=$(basename "$f")

  # Route by filename: anything containing 'platform' (case-insensitive) →
  # platform DB; everything else → main DB.
  case "$fname" in
    *platform*|*Platform*)
      target_url="${PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL:-$DATABASE_URL}"
      target_name="platform"
      ;;
    *)
      target_url="$DATABASE_URL"
      target_name="main"
      ;;
  esac

  if apply_one "$target_url" "$target_name" "$f"; then
    applied_count=$((applied_count + 1))
  else
    failed_count=$((failed_count + 1))
  fi
done

echo "Summary: applied=$applied_count failed=$failed_count"

if [ "$failed_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "WARN: $failed_count migration(s) failed (see logs above). Pre-existing"
  echo "schema-drift migrations (e.g. 002 expected verification_policies.scope_id"
  echo "that doesn't exist on the live schema) are non-blocking — the app's"
  echo "startup-migrations.ts has its own retry path. Exiting 0 so docker"
  echo "compose dependent services can recreate; otherwise --force-recreate"
  echo "would block on migrations service_completed_successfully condition."
  echo "(BACKLOG #6 — partial-failure exit semantics.)"
fi

echo "Migration runner finished (applied=$applied_count, failed=$failed_count)."
exit 0

# =============================================================================
# The defect: with an empty SERVICES_TABLE, `docker-build.sh all` died at the
# banner's `${BUILD_LIST[*]}` with `BUILD_LIST[*]: unbound variable` under
# bash 3.2 + `set -u` — three lines after the `[ -n ]` guard added for exactly
# this class. That guard works (BUILD_LIST is left genuinely empty); the display
# expansion after it does not. And `${BUILD_LIST[*]:-}` alone only moves the
# death 55 lines down to the parallel loop's `"${BUILD_LIST[@]}"` — measured —
# so the shape that holds is a guard on `${#BUILD_LIST[@]}` that names the
# table and exits before either.
#
# docker is NEVER run: a stub on a private PATH records every call and exits 0,
# so the control cells can prove the working path still builds without a
# daemon. The empty table is produced by a fixture COPY of the subject whose
# heredoc body is stripped — the table is a literal inside the script, so
# there is no other way to reach the path — and the copy's row count is
# asserted 29 -> 0 before the cell is scored.
#
# Round 2 (KS-877, the tier-2 gate's F1): CELL 3 was RED on the repository's CI
# (ubuntu, bash 5.x) while green on macOS — `docker-build.sh`'s `((RUNNING++))`
# exits 1 when RUNNING is 0, and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` (COMPAT item 45) kills the
# script on it; bash 3.2 does not. CELL 4 pins the construct's ABSENCE statically
# (this box has no bash >= 4.1; CI's CELL 3 is the runtime instrument) and CELL 5
# proves the fix does not swallow a genuine build failure. The summary line
# carries the cell count (`(of N cells)`) and the run FAILS if fewer cells ran.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh
#        DOCKER_BUILD_SH=/path/to/other/docker-build.sh bash …   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=5

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
# Same subject discipline as orchestrate_jobs.test.sh (KS-923 F2 / KS-941).
if [ "${DOCKER_BUILD_SH+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$DOCKER_BUILD_SH" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is set but EMPTY — refusing to silently grade the shipped script." >&2
  exit 2
fi
SUBJ="${DOCKER_BUILD_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: docker-build.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks877.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Data rows of the SERVICES_TABLE heredoc in a script: tab-separated, not a
# comment. The same predicate service_names() applies.
table_rows() {
  sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$1" \
    | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# Build a fixture project root around a copy of the script under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = table: intact | emptied
# The copy lives at <root>/scripts/docker-build.sh so the script's own
# `PROJECT_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."` resolves to the fixture root.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" table="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/scripts" "$root/bin" "$root/services/auth"
  printf 'FROM scratch\n' > "$root/services/auth/Dockerfile"
  if [ "$table" = emptied ]; then
    # Strip every line between the heredoc's opening and closing markers.
    sed "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/{//!d;}" "$SUBJ" > "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  else
    cp "$SUBJ" "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  fi
  # docker stub: records every call, succeeds.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\nexit 0\n' "$root"; } > "$root/bin/docker"
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker"
}

# Run the copy with ONLY the stub dir in front of the system dirs. Prints rc.
run_build() {
  local root="$1"; shift
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"; cd "$root" && bash scripts/docker-build.sh "$@" ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
build_calls() { if [ -f "$1/docker_calls.txt" ]; then grep -c '^docker build' "$1/docker_calls.txt" || true; else echo 0; fi; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — KS-877. THE REGRESSION. An EMPTY table must be refused by name —
# "no services matched", naming SERVICES_TABLE — with NO `unbound variable`
# and no build attempted. Asserted on rc = 1 AND the ABSENCE of the
# unbound-variable death AND the PRESENCE of the message naming SERVICES_TABLE
# AND 0 builds. rc alone cannot discriminate base from head (both exit 1),
# which is why the other three clauses exist; it is asserted so that a guard
# that prints the message and then exits 0 still reds (the gate's Tk). The row
# count is a precondition: a copy that still has rows would pass the pre-fix
# script and say nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/empty" emptied
rows_subj="$(table_rows "$SUBJ")"; rows_copy="$(table_rows "$WORK/empty/scripts/docker-build.sh")"
if [ "$rows_subj" -lt 1 ] || [ "$rows_copy" -ne 0 ]; then
  bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
      "precondition broken: subject rows=$rows_subj (expected >=1), emptied copy rows=$rows_copy (expected 0) — the cell cannot discriminate"
else
  rc_empty="$(run_build "$WORK/empty" all)"
  if [ "$rc_empty" = 1 ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/empty")" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE ($rows_subj rows -> $rows_copy) is refused by name — 'no services matched', naming SERVICES_TABLE — with no 'unbound variable', 0 builds, rc=$rc_empty"
  else
    bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
        "rc=$rc_empty, unbound variable present=$(grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo YES || echo no), message present=$(grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), table named=$(grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/empty"), last lines: $(tail -2 "$WORK/empty/out.txt" | sed 's|.*/scripts/||' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL (the working path, one service). The intact table with
# `auth` must still print `Services:  auth`, build it once via the stub, report
# BUILD OK and exit 0. Without this, CELL 1 could pass by a guard that refuses
# every list.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/one" intact
rc_one="$(run_build "$WORK/one" auth)"
if [ "$rc_one" = 0 ] && grep -q '^  Services:  auth$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" && grep -q '\[auth\] BUILD OK' "$WORK/one/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/one")" -eq 1 ] && grep -q -- '-f services/auth/Dockerfile' "$WORK/one/docker_calls.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' prints 'Services:  auth', builds it once (-f services/auth/Dockerfile), BUILD OK, rc 0"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' still builds it once and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_one, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/one"), output: $(grep -v '^=*$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" | tail -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — CONTROL (the working path, every service, the parallel loop). The
# intact table with `all` must build every row via the stub and exit 0 — the
# path whose re-index guard (`${#PIDS[@]}`) the file's own comment documents,
# exercised under bash 3.2 with instant builds so the loop's empty-array case
# is actually reached.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/all" intact
rc_all="$(run_build "$WORK/all" all)"
if [ "$rc_all" = 0 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj):" "$WORK/all/out.txt" && grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/all/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/all")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/all/out.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj), rc 0, no unbound variable"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_all, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/all") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED' "$WORK/all/out.txt" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — KS-877 round 2 (the gate's F1). The subject has NO bare
# arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement (`((X++))` / `((X--))` on a line
# of its own). Such a command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0 — a
# post-increment yields the OLD value, so `((RUNNING++))` at RUNNING=0 "fails"
# — and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` exits on it (bash COMPAT item 45: "Bash-4.1 …
# exits when any command fails, not just a simple command or pipeline").
# bash 3.2 (macOS) does not, which is why CELL 3 was green here and RED on CI's
# ubuntu (run 34743050388: `rc=1, builds=0 of 29` — the script died after
# backgrounding ONE build). This is a STATIC pin, honest about being one: the
# runtime pin is CELL 3 on a bash >= 4.1, i.e. CI. The positive control inside
# the cell proves the grep can fire (a here-string holding `((X++))` -> 1).
# `[[:space:]]`, not `\s`: BSD grep.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARITH_RE='^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$'
arith_control="$(printf '  ((X++))\n' | grep -cE "$ARITH_RE" || true)"
arith_hits="$(grep -nE "$ARITH_RE" "$SUBJ" || true)"
arith_count="$(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | grep -c . || true)"
if [ "$arith_control" != 1 ]; then
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "instrument cannot fire: the positive control read $arith_control (expected 1) — the cell is not scoring the subject"
elif [ "$arith_count" -eq 0 ]; then
  ok "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement — ((X++)) exits 1 at 0 and bash >= 4.1 set -e dies on it (control fires: $arith_control)"
else
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "count=$arith_count (control=$arith_control): $(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | sed 's/^\([0-9]*\):[[:space:]]*/:\1 /' | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 5 — KS-877 round 2, the MASK CONTROL. A run where ONE build genuinely
# fails must still land in `FAILED (1)` with rc 1 and the summary printed —
# the counter fix must not swallow a real failure. A second stub records the
# call, then exits 1 when its args name services/auth/Dockerfile (asserted
# unique among the table's rows). On bash 3.2 this reads the SAME before and
# after the fix — that IS the control: the fix changes nothing 3.2 can see
# except the arithmetic status; on CI (bash 5.x) it exercises the fixed loop
# under a genuine failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/onefail" intact
{ printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\ncase "$*" in *services/auth/Dockerfile*) exit 1;; esac\nexit 0\n' "$WORK/onefail"; } > "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
chmod +x "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
auth_rows="$(sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$WORK/onefail/scripts/docker-build.sh" \
  | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ && $2 == "services/auth/Dockerfile"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$auth_rows" -ne 1 ]; then
  bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
      "precondition broken: $auth_rows table rows resolve to services/auth/Dockerfile (expected exactly 1) — the failing stub cannot be aimed"
else
  rc_onefail="$(run_build "$WORK/onefail" all)"
  if [ "$rc_onefail" = 1 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))):" "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && grep -q 'FAILED (1):' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && grep -q '^    auth$' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && ! grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt"; then
    ok "MASK CONTROL — with the auth stub exiting 1, 'all' still runs every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))), FAILED (1): auth, rc 1"
  else
    bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
        "rc=$rc_onefail, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED\|All builds' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass (KS-877 round 2): the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE — %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
